solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: French writer presenting emperor's empire in novel form

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A French author offers a novel about an emperor's realm.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of EMPERORS EMPIRE gives the author of Carmen; 'presenting' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineteenth-century novelist who wrote Carmen and Colomba was a Frenchman of letters.

clue.text: Discount, third off? Er, could be

definitions.text: Discount, third off? Er, could be

indicators.note: could be suggests another possible form of the letters
the third letter of the word discount is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a discount means a third off the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third off' drops S from DISCOUNT, leaving DICOUNT, and 'could be' rearranges that with ER. The whole clue also defines: a third off is a cut in price.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount such as a third off the price is a cut in cost.

clue.text: Ready to grab guy rope

indicators.note: to grab is to seize, so one piece clutches the other

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
he refers to a male, a guy

explanation.surface: Get set to seize a guy rope on a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy rope' looks like one tent fitting; 'guy' gives HE and 'rope' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing boat a sheet is the rope controlling a sail's angle.

clue.text: First off, in autumn this happens to bug

indicators.note: first off means remove the opening letter

parts.note: in autumn the leaves drop from the trees

explanation.surface: An observation about falling foliage in the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' removes L from LEAVES DROP.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug a conversation is to listen in secretly, as a spy would.

clue.text: Maiden's heart regularly broken by Yankee? I don't believe it!

indicators.note: broken by means split open with something inserted

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word heart

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A maiden's heart is broken by an American and her friend is astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives HAT from 'heart'; 'broken by' puts Y between M and HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: This old exclamation expresses disbelief or surprise, like 'well I never'.

clue.text: Gets new Dutch residence to house girl around west end of Rotterdam

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the rest goes inside
around means the girl's name surrounds the next letter

parts.note: Marie is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, the west end of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Dutch home in Rotterdam where a girl lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is old Cockney slang for a wife ('my old Dutch'), not the nationality, so the definition means taking a new wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a new wife is marrying again, since Dutch is slang for one's spouse.

clue.text: Fruit mostly heading off endemic skin disease

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: a mango is a tropical fruit

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Most fruit is cut off by a widespread disease of the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MANGO to MANG; 'heading off' takes E from 'endemic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mange is a mite-caused skin condition in animals, causing hair loss.

clue.text: Rider's still on time to meet royal

parts.note: still in the sense 'still more' means even
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A rider is waiting quietly in time to meet a member of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Rider's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse or rider competing in three-day eventing.

clue.text: Mirror perhaps reflects earthenware article, one from Dresden?

indicators.note: reflects means mirrors, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a pot is an earthenware vessel
der is a German word for the, one way of saying the in Dresden

explanation.surface: A mirror shows the reflection of a pot made in Dresden.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper; 'reflects' turns POTDER around.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabloid newspapers like the Daily Mirror are called this for their red mastheads.

clue.text: Invest with last dollar finally spent

indicators.note: spent means used up and gone, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to last is to endure, to go on

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word dollar

explanation.surface: Someone puts their final dollar into an investment and it is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from 'dollar', and 'spent' removes it from ENDURE, leaving ENDUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue someone is to invest or endow them with a quality, an old literary verb.

clue.text: Forcefulness shown by macho types overwhelming centre of European city

indicators.note: the macho types swamp and replace the middle letters of the city name

parts.note: Venice is the Italian city of canals
he-men are macho, muscular types

explanation.surface: Tough guys take over the heart of a European city with great force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelming centre of' replaces NI, the middle of VENICE, with HEMEN, giving VE-HEMEN-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehemence is passionate intensity of feeling or expression, which is forcefulness.

clue.text: Historian can be understood by you and me

parts.note: something tacit is implied and understood without being stated
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A historian's meaning is plain to the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman historian who wrote the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: Harrow's wrong to take on older boys

indicators.note: take on here means to take in or admit, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
older boys grow into men

explanation.surface: A report on the famous English public school Harrow letting older pupils bully.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school, but here it is the verb, to distress; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow someone is to distress them greatly, a synonym for causing anguish.

clue.text: From bustling airport take off at — at an earlier time

indicators.note: a bustling place is busy and stirred up, so the letters are mixed
take off tells us to remove the letters of the word at from the mix

explanation.surface: A traveller in a busy airport is told to take off at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange AIRPORT, then 'take off' removes A and T, leaving I, R, P, O, R to be arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior is an adjective meaning earlier, so occurring before in time.

clue.text: Note, drip's captivated by heart- throb — that's disgusting!

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: captivated means held captive, so it goes inside

parts.note: the pulse is the throb of the heart
IV is short for an intravenous drip; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A girl's wet friend falls for a pin-up, which her friend finds revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart-throb' suggests a pin-up idol, but it means the heartbeat; 'drip' is the hospital kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive arouses intense disgust or revulsion.

clue.text: Dog expert vows initially to stop terrier barking

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so these letters go inside
barking means mad, so the letters of terrier are scrambled
initially points to the first letters of expert and vows

explanation.surface: A specialist promises to quieten a terrier that keeps yapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' (mad) gives RETRIER; 'Dog expert' tempts as a vet, but 'Dog' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a gun-dog breed trained to fetch shot game.

clue.text: Man batting after Jack gets 3

indicators.note: after places the man's name behind the sailor

parts.note: a jack, like a tar, is a sailor
Paul is a man's name
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: A batsman follows a sailor into the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '3' refers to the answer at 3 down, a sailing rope, but here a large waterproof cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a large waterproof covering cloth, matching the answer to 3 down.

clue.text: Composer firmly holds piano should go — it may affect the brass

parts.note: Verdi was the Italian opera composer

indicators.note: should go says that letter is dropped

parts.note: grips means holds firmly
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A composer clutches a piano that must leave, while the brass section suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' looks like the orchestra's brass section, matching 'Composer' and 'piano', but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdigris is the green patina that forms on copper, bronze and brass.

clue.text: Flyer's first person booted out by aircrew, primarily for rough stuff

indicators.note: one letter is kicked out and the other takes its place

parts.note: a sandpiper is a wading bird, so a flyer; the 's stands for is
I is the first person pronoun

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of aircrew

explanation.surface: A passenger is thrown off a plane by the cabin crew for rough behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booted out by' swaps I in SANDPIPER for A, the first letter of 'aircrew'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpaper is abrasive paper, rough material used for smoothing wood.

clue.text: Perhaps The Sun's for people like me

definitions.meaning: the sun goes down each evening, so it is one example of things that go down
me is the person who compiled the crossword

explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, suggesting its puzzle compilers, but here it is the sun in the sky, which sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who compose crosswords are known by this name, as the compiler is.

clue.text: Cancel loan, needing to secure credit

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a sub is an advance or loan of money
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Writing off a loan needs some credit to back it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for cancelling or abandoning it.

clue.text: Pub brawl in northern town

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a row is a noisy quarrel or brawl

explanation.surface: A pub fight breaks out in a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Cumbria, north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow-in-Furness is a shipbuilding town in Cumbria in the north of England.

clue.text: "Play gooseberry" perhaps has no name in foreign language

indicators.note: has no says that letter is missing

parts.note: to play gooseberry is to be an unwanted third person, to tag along with a couple

explanation.surface: Playing the unwanted third wheel leaves someone nameless abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'play gooseberry' is the British idiom for being an unwanted third person on a couple's outing, hence TAG ALONG; 'has no' removes N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the language of the Philippines, the basis of Filipino.

clue.text: On ship clog dancing's avoided by Charlie Sheen

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged
avoided by means the named letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: Clog dancing on board ship is shunned by the actor Charlie Sheen.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Sheen the actor is a red herring: 'Charlie' is C and 'Sheen' is the definition. Rearranging CLOG without C gives GLO, sitting on SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is a soft lustre on a surface, a synonym of shine.

clue.text: Note is included in contracts for convenience

indicators.note: included in means placed inside

parts.note: to contract an illness is to get it

explanation.surface: A note is written into the contracts for convenience.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public convenience is a public toilet, and the men's is signed this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A convenience in British usage is a public toilet, here the men's.

clue.text: Vexed, in rage that's greater, ultimately

definitions.text: Vexed, in rage that's greater, ultimately

indicators.note: vexed means troubled or agitated, so the letters are stirred up
ultimately points to the final letter of greater

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed ends up in an even greater fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vexed' rearranges IN RAGE to ANGRIE, and 'ultimately' adds R, the end of 'greater'. The whole clue also describes being more cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Being vexed and in a greater rage is being more cross, the comparative of furious.

clue.text: An enormous number denied a love for this Russian writer

indicators.note: denied means refused, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a googol is ten to the power of a hundred
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A Russian author is refused vast sums of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' removes one O from GOOGOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the Russian author of Dead Souls and The Overcoat.

clue.text: Moving book about uninitated woman with little learning

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: without its initial means the first letter goes

parts.note: Fiona is a woman's name
L, for learner, is the short form for someone learning

explanation.surface: A moving book about a woman with only a little education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives EMOT and 'uninitated' (so printed) leaves IONA; L for learner is the convention from L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving stirs the feelings, which is the sense of emotional.

clue.text: Somewhat vulgar Bollywood film star? Yes and no

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather crude Indian film star, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: Greta Garbo was a Hollywood star, not a Bollywood one: hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood screen legend of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: My slant, say, set out to incorporate streamlining first of all?

definitions.text: My slant, say, set out to incorporate streamlining first of all?

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take in, so that letter goes inside
out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
first of all points to the opening letter of streamlining

explanation.surface: Someone explains their approach of making streamlining the top priority.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram makes SYTEMANALYST, which 'to incorporate' fills with S. The surface's slant is indeed what such a professional brings: streamlining.
explanation.definitionFit: A computing professional who analyses processes to make them efficient, i.e. one who streamlines working methods.
